correctness.rationale: Reconstructed path-algebra multiplication e_u e_v=δ_uv e_v, e_s α=α, αe_t=α, αβ=0; ordered pairwise-zero equations force each vertex diagonal m-vector either zero or one nonzero color (including m=1). For arrow α:s→t, if both endpoint diagonal vectors vanish its m arrow coordinates are unconstrained; otherwise equations give exactly one free arrow parameter (also for loops, opposing arrows, different endpoint colors and char2). Thus each labeled stratum is (G_m)^(n-|S|)×A^(h+(m-1)e_Q(S)); summing Fq points yields formula, maximum dimension and count of top-dimensional irreducible closures. The empty subset gives δ>=0, threshold (m-1)ρ>1. At fixed q, N_m=Σ_e q^(me)P_e(m) uniquely recovers exponent e and polynomial coefficients by dominant exponential separation, with max e=h and max polynomial degree n, hence Xi_Q; no graph isomorphism claim. Independently exhaustive F2 counts 4 (isolated vertex,m3),14 (loop,m3),38 (one arrow,m3),48 (parallel arrows,m2), all match formula. F4 implemented in source checker but not independently tested; proof field independent.

originality.rationale: Quiver radical-square-zero algebra and its representation-variety components are well-known (Bleher–Chinburg–Huisgen-Zimmermann), but those moduli classify modules, not arbitrary ordered zero-product tuples of algebra elements. Huang counts mutually annihilating unrestricted square matrices, principally pairs, not arbitrary m in every radical-square-zero quiver algebra. Existing induced-subgraph component polynomial records component count rather than induced-edge count; Xi_Q is not newly named as a graph polynomial. No stronger prior result was identified implying all-arity point count, top-component/density law and fixed-field inverse polynomial recovery.
residual_risks: Only reduced variety and top-dimensional irreducible components classified; lower-dimensional components and nilpotent scheme structure not asserted.
